note: Prices are a rough guide for a party of 3 (2 adults + 1 child). Opening hours on the islands are seasonal and change often — check before making a special journey. Many places close on Sundays, especially on Lewis and Harris.

places.name: Café Arriba
places.description: Buzzy, colourful café up Quay Brae with harbour glimpses. All-day breakfasts, burgers, big salads and great cakes; local and fair-trade ingredients, with GF choices marked.

places.name: Relish
places.description: Small café-deli on Wentworth Street known for coeliac-safe fish and chips from a separate fryer, plus rolls, coffee and cakes. GF items clearly marked and staff know their stuff.

places.name: The Chippy (Portree Harbour)
places.description: Classic harbour-side fish and chips — eat them on the pier wall watching the boats (guard them from the gulls). Takeaway only, so the dog can join you.

places.name: Isle of Skye Baking Company
places.description: Bakery-café famous for 'lunch bread' (a meal baked inside a loaf), with gluten-free bakes and cakes usually available, plus a craft shop attached.

places.name: The Isles Inn
places.description: Traditional flagstone-and-fire pub on Somerled Square with hearty portions, local ales and regular live folk music. Dogs welcome in the bar.

places.name: Sligachan Hotel — Seumas' Bar
places.description: Legendary climbers' bar under the Cuillin with 400+ whiskies, its own Cuillin Brewery, big pub grub menu (GF options marked) and a children's play area. Dogs welcome.
places.hours: Daily, food all day in season

places.name: The Old Inn
places.description: Whitewashed free house on the shore of Loch Harport, minutes from Talisker Distillery. Local seafood and ales, waterside terrace, live trad music Thursdays. Dogs welcome in the pub.
places.hours: Daily from noon, food lunch & dinner

places.name: The Oyster Shed
places.description: Farm shop and takeaway above Loch Harport shucking its own oysters — plus langoustines, crab, scallops and chips at shack prices. Outdoor picnic benches, so dogs are fine.

places.name: The Stein Inn
places.description: Skye's oldest inn (1790), right on the Waternish shore — a perfect sunset pint. Seafood-leaning menu; children welcome, dogs welcome except 6–9pm in the food service area.

places.name: Café Sia
places.description: Wood-fired pizza and own-roasted coffee with Red Cuillin views. Gluten-free bases and a proper kids' menu; dog-friendly seating in the covered outdoor area.

places.name: The Edinbane Inn
places.description: Cosy session-music pub between Portree and Dunvegan; seasonal menu strong on local seafood with GF options flagged. Trad sessions several nights a week; dogs welcome in the bar.
places.hours: Daily in season, food lunch & dinner

places.name: Deli Gasta
places.description: Deli-café in the old mill by Broadford Bay: doorstep toasties, home bakes, good coffee and picnic supplies, with GF bakes usually on the counter.

places.name: Single Track
places.description: Tiny Grand Designs-featured espresso bar and gallery at the top of the Trotternish loop. Exceptional coffee and cakes (always a GF bake); outdoor tables suit dogs.

places.name: The Boatshed
places.description: Stornoway's smartest table, overlooking the harbour: island seafood, Stornoway black pudding and Hebridean lamb, with GF-adaptable dishes. A treat night rather than a cheap one.

places.name: Kopi Java
places.description: Family-run coffee house on Cromwell Street with harbour and Lews Castle views — strong coffee, simple lunches and generous cakes.

places.name: The Blue Lobster
places.description: Charming little harbour-front café — proper coffee, homemade cakes and window seats for boat-watching. Dogs welcome.

places.name: The Hub Café (Glen House)
places.description: Friendly 24-seat café at Glen House with the same menu to sit in or take away. Notably coeliac-aware (cross-contamination taken seriously), vegan options, and dog friendly.

places.name: Mollans Takeaway
places.description: Takeaway chippy where almost everything is gluten free (burger buns and macaroni aside) — a rare safe fish supper for coeliacs. Eat by the harbour; takeaway suits the dog.

places.name: The Crown Inn
places.description: Harbour-front inn with a proper public bar and a lounge doing dependable pub classics and local seafood. Dogs welcome in the bar area.

places.name: An Lanntair Café Bar
places.description: Bright café-bar in the arts centre opposite the ferry pier — soups, flatbreads and bakes with GF choices marked, plus a cinema and galleries to entertain kids on wet days.

places.name: Eleven (Caladh Inn)
places.description: Family-friendly hotel restaurant known for its good-value buffet and carvery — an easy refuel with fussy eaters, and one of the few places open on Sundays.

places.name: Uig Sands Restaurant
places.description: Destination dining in a glass-fronted room over Uig Sands — set seafood-led menus from the day's landings. Kids welcome (the beach below is the pre-dinner entertainment).

places.name: Loch Croistean Coffee Shop
places.description: Converted schoolhouse café on the Uig road: soups, seafood specials and famous home baking in front of the stove. A welcome stop on the way to the beaches.

places.name: Café Sonas
places.description: Bright community café above the harbour at the island's northern tip — paninis, fish and chips, and cakes (GF options usually available). Handy for the Butt of Lewis.

places.name: Machair Kitchen (Talla na Mara)
places.description: Community-owned centre above Niseaboist beach near Luskentyre — chowders, crab rolls and bakes with the best lunch view on Harris. GF aware; dogs welcome on the terrace.

places.name: North Harbour Bistro
places.description: Acclaimed little bistro over the causeway on Scalpay — beautifully presented local seafood at fair prices. GF-adaptable; worth the detour alone.

places.name: Croft 36
places.description: A tiny roadside honesty shed stocked daily with crab soup, langoustine rolls, pies and puddings from the croft — leave your money in the box. Get there early; it sells out.
places.hours: Daytime until sold out, closed Sun

places.name: The Anchorage
places.description: Relaxed harbourside restaurant-bar by the Leverburgh pier — seafood platters, fish and chips and a pint while you watch the Uist ferry come in. Dogs welcome in the bar/outside.

places.name: The Butty Bus
places.description: The famous stationary bus by the Leverburgh pier — burgers, bacon rolls and fish and chips while you queue for the Uist ferry. Cash-friendly, dog-tolerant, zero pretension.

places.name: Harris Hotel
places.description: Tarbert institution (est. 1865) — J.M. Barrie etched his initials in a window. Bar meals and a dining room with GF options marked; dogs welcome in the bar and garden.

places.name: Hotel Hebrides — Mote Bar
places.description: Steps from the Tarbert ferry ramp — seafood chowder, burgers and local gins in the buzzy Mote Bar. Handy for a pre-boarding pint; dogs welcome in the bar.

places.name: Loomshed Brewery Taproom
places.description: Harris's own microbrewery on the edge of Tarbert — Iasgair lager and Poacher ale brewed with island water, pizzas some evenings. Seasonal opening; dogs welcome in the taproom.

places.name: Skoon Art Café
places.description: Gallery-café on the Golden Road famous for soup, cake (GF usually among them) and paintings of the Bays. Tue–Sat in season — a perfect Golden Road pit stop.
